punchline: Prometheus brings SmolVLM-assisted inspection into physical action: a working robot sorter, simulation environment and Intel learning stack.
description:
## Prometheus: robots that inspect and act
Prometheus brings visual intelligence into physical action on an SO-101 robot station. Our ambition is adaptable inspection for smaller factories: reuse a compact station, teach new parts and make robot behavior inspectable.

## Working physical demonstration
The updated video shows SmolVLM-assisted vision-guided sorting on the real robot, using overhead, wrist and close camera views. The supplied recording reports three completed good-to-blue sorts and a 48-second median cycle time. The full physical footage plays at 3x speed with normal-speed narration.

This is a selected working demonstration, not a broad reliability benchmark. The recording marks inspection confidence as partial and does not demonstrate the defective-to-green branch. SmolVLM assists the vision-guided execution path; it is distinct from the SmolVLA action-policy experiments.

## Completed system components
We implemented the station application, perception and inspection tools, motion/control utilities, a customized Physical AI Studio dashboard, OpenVINO inference checks, and bounded-output and stop paths. The system connects visual observations to decisions and physical execution, with source and evidence included for review.

Our MuJoCo environment supports expert collection, contact/action traces, replay and LeRobot export. The video also includes a successful simulated pickup-and-placement sequence, clearly labeled as an expert-controller simulation.

## Robot learning pipeline
The implemented data pipeline prepares 64 real demonstrations with corrected task labels, train-only normalization and reset-family splits: 41 training, 12 validation and 11 test episodes. We built 32 experiment configurations comparing ACT and SmolVLA, normal images and causal target-X conditioning, four augmentation recipes, and real-only versus mixed real/simulation data.

The X cue starts from a chosen target and disappears on tracking loss. Online augmentation changes training images without treating copies as independent demonstrations. Real-data training has launched; the full comparison and mixed-data transfer validation remain in progress. The physical video demonstrates the SmolVLM-assisted path, not a claim that learned-policy task success is solved.

## What comes next
Expand the physical evaluation across defective parts, shifted objects and clutter. Use the same evaluation scenes to measure learned-policy transfer and select which augmentation and synthetic-data variants genuinely improve execution. Prometheus already delivers the working physical demonstration, simulation environment and reproducible pipeline needed for that next step.
